title: Hint-driven oppath orchestrator for prefill-decode routing (arch+seqlen flavoring)
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, hint-driven orchestration layer that picks the execution pathway (kernel variant + quantization fallback + prefill vs decode routing) per-request by combining a compact architecture fingerprint with per-customer sequence-length distributions. This is intended to reduce p95/p99 latency tail and cost regressions for mixed prefill/decode workloads without expensive per-request probing.

Background: Our runtime currently chooses kernels primarily by static heuristics (GPU type + model) and occasional microbench probes. That approach struggles for customers with mixed short/long prefills, and heterogeneous instance fleets where optimized kernels trade cost for tail latency. Existing autotuners either probe too aggressively (wasting cycles) or are too conservative (miss optimal kernels).

Proposed approach: Implement a Hint-Driven OPath (Execution-Path) Orchestrator with three core components:
1) Flavoring: compute a lightweight "flavor score" per request that combines: GPU fingerprint (SM/compute capability, chiplet topology), model op-family fingerprint (attention pattern, kv cache size estimate), and an on-device sequence-length estimated bucket (short/medium/long) derived from prompt metadata and historical session distribution.
2) Policy table: a compact table mapping flavor buckets to preferred kernel variants (fast-prefill kernel, decode-optimized kernel, safety-fallback quantized kernel). Each entry includes: preferred kernel id, probe budget (if unknown), throttle policy for probes, and latency safety bands.
3) Probing & warmstart: for low-confidence flavor buckets we allow limited microprobes using small synthetic inputs or short real requests in a controlled budget. Probe results seed a warmstart cache and update policy confidence.

Safety and fallbacks: enforced safety bands ensure that if a chosen path exceeds p99 latency or error thresholds, we immediately switch to safer kernel variants and mark the policy entry for re-evaluation. Rollbacks are automated via rollout controller.

Success metrics:
- Reduce p95 latency for mixed prefill/decode workloads by >= 15% on test fleet.
- Keep p99 latency at or below existing baseline (no regressions).
- Average cost per token delta <= +5% (goal: neutral or negative).
- Probe budget overhead < 2% of throughput for new flavor buckets.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/runtime/hint-driven-opath-orchestrator
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345
- Bench harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-bench/tree/feature/flavor-prober

Telemetry and observability: add standardized labels to runtime telemetry: flavor_id, kernel_variant, probe_attempted, probe_latency_ms, latency_ms, tail_percentile_label. Dashboards: per-flavor p50/p95/p99 and per-kernel cost breakdown.

Testing plan: staged rollout on canary capacity, synthetic bench with customer-like seqlen mixes, shadow routing for 2 weeks, then gradual 10->25->50% rollouts with rollback triggers based on p99 and error-rate thresholds.

Risks: incorrect flavor mapping could cause oscillations; probe storms if not budgeted; increased complexity in policy management. Mitigations: global probe budget, circuit-breaker on per-flavor instability, nightly policy pruning job.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Priya Nair: Kicked off discovery. Collected seq-len histograms from top 20 customers; found bimodal distributions for three customers that explain poor kernel choices in baseline.

2026-02-20 - Ethan Cole: Implemented minimal flavor fingerprint (gpu_family + model_family + seqlen_bucket). Initial microbench shows 12% p95 improvement on single-GPU tests when picking prefill-specialized kernels for short prefills.
2026-02-24 - Design review (Sofia Ramirez): Recommend adding explicit 'probe_ttl' for cache entries and a per-customer override to force conservative choices for enterprise SLAs.

2026-03-01 - Marcus Li (runtime): Code review feedback on PR#12345: tighten concurrency control around warmstart cache to avoid double-probing under high QPS; suggested metrics for probe_cost and probe_success_rate.

2026-03-04 - QA tests (Daniel Kim): Shadow routing run (48h) completed. Observed regression in p99 for a rare long-seqlen workload when using mixed-kernel combo. Temporary mitigation: increase safety band and mark that flavor as 'no-probe' until we add longer-prefill kernel variant.
2026-03-08 - Ethan Cole: Updated policy table format to include 'safety_decay' and 'probe_backoff' fields. Added canary config for autonomous rollback when p99 exceeds baseline by 10% for 5m.
2026-03-10 - Priya Nair: Preparing rollout plan. Need approvals from SRE and Product before starting 10% traffic ramp. Added performance checklist and rollout playbook to Confluence.
next_steps: 1) Finalize policy table schema and persistence. 2) Implement probe budget controller and telemetry hooks. 3) Run 72h shadow on canary fleet, iterate on failing flavors. 4) Request SRE approval for gradual rollout.
notes: This ticket focuses on orchestration heuristics and low-cost probing; it intentionally avoids changes to kernel implementations themselves. If we discover missing kernel variants, create follow-up ENG tickets for kernel engineer teams.
